spans.claim: Seton Darville is a popular English novelist and secret service chief
spans.anchor: Charles Seton Darville. In every bookshop and bookstall
spans.span: The thick-set Englishman, smiling and care-free, was one of the most popular of English novelists, whose name was known in every country throughout the world, Charles Seton Darville. In every bookshop and bookstall on the five continents his works were sold, for they were translated into many languages, even into Arabic and Chinese.

spans.claim: Joan Caborn is involved in espionage and deception
spans.anchor: Joan Caborn, whom he had first met at winter sports
spans.span: He was puzzled by Joan Caborn, whom he had first met at winter sports at Wengen, in Switzerland, the previous winter.

spans.claim: George Caborn is a foreign-born businessman and spy
spans.anchor: George Caborn, the woman’s husband. Though he bore an English name
spans.span: He was George Caborn, the woman's husband. Though he bore an English name he was undoubtedly a Southerner, but that was explained by the fact that his grandfather had been an English merchant who had settled in Athens.

spans.claim: Darville suspects Joan and George Caborn of a desperate errand
spans.anchor: They are over here on a very desperate errand
spans.span: They are over here on a very desperate errand, so we must find them, and defeat their activities.

spans.claim: Darville disables the electrical detonators on the explosives
spans.anchor: He gummed those little discs of paper upon the electrical terminals

spans.claim: Explosives were attached to the Forth Bridge in rubber hot-water bottles
spans.anchor: rubber hot-water bottles filled to their utmost capacity
spans.span: In the center of the bed in the back room of the first floor lay four new rubber hot-water bottles filled to their utmost capacity.

spans.claim: A motor boat carrying the saboteurs explodes after a gunfight
spans.anchor: there was a bright red flash, and an explosion so terrific
spans.span: Suddenly the crackle of a machine-gun mounted on the pursuing boat was heard, and the next moment, from the first boat, there was a bright red flash, and an explosion so terrific that more than twenty houses on the shore of the firth were wrecked, happily without any loss of life.

spans.claim: Edris Temperley is secretly engaged to Karl Weiss
spans.anchor: Edris, though pretending to be his, had engaged herself to Karl

spans.claim: Karl Weiss is offered a secret mission to Russia by the British Secret Service
spans.anchor: Karl Weiss presented himself at a certain room in the War Office
spans.span: THE TRAP At ten o'clock on Thursday morning Karl Weiss presented himself at a certain room in the War Office, as he had been requested by letter, and there found a grave, gray-haired official awaiting him.

spans.claim: Darville orders interception and copying of Edris and Karl’s correspondence
spans.anchor: I want all outgoing and incoming correspondence examined, copied
spans.span: Make a note that I want all outgoing and incoming correspondence examined, copied, and sent to me of two persons.

spans.claim: Edris writes affectionate letters to Karl Weiss while deceiving Darville
spans.anchor: Edris’s letter breathed an undying devotion
spans.span: Edris's letter breathed an undying devotion, and told her lover that, to her delight, Darville was leaving Stagsden.

spans.claim: Darville confronts Edris with her betrayal and engagement to Karl
spans.anchor: You are lying to me--deceived me until this very moment!

spans.claim: Karl Weiss threatens Darville and asserts his claim on Edris
spans.anchor: He placed his hand upon his hip-pocket, where he had his automatic pistol
spans.span: he said threateningly, and he placed his hand upon his hip-pocket, where he had his automatic pistol, in order to frighten her.

spans.claim: Darville arranges a trap by employing Karl Weiss on a secret mission
spans.anchor: We shall find some way out, Forbes. We’ve never been beaten yet
spans.span: We shall find some way out, Forbes. We've never been beaten yet.

spans.claim: Karl Weiss accepts the mission and leaves England
spans.anchor: his proposed mission was canceled, his services not being required
spans.span: That same afternoon, while Edris and Darville were in the train returning to Stagsden, Karl Weiss received a letter, delivered by messenger, informing him with regret that the matter referred to at his interview had been satisfactorily cleared up, and, such being the circumstances, his proposed mission was canceled, his services not being required.

spans.claim: Edris and Darville reconcile after her confession and remorse
spans.anchor: I have discarded him, Seti, and I have returned to you
spans.span: I have discarded him, Seti, and I have returned to you, if--if I dare face you again.

spans.claim: The sabotage plot is foiled and the Caborns are killed
spans.anchor: the plotters themselves have lost their lives in their desperate attempt
spans.span: Through the vigilance of the authorities the gigantic bridge has been saved from destruction, though the plotters themselves have lost their lives in their desperate attempt to put the bridge in readiness for destruction at any moment.

spans.claim: Darville’s dual nature as a novelist and secret service chief
spans.anchor: Seton Darville possessed two separate and distinct personalities

spans.span: There has been no telegram to-day, monsieur," replied the man with the crossed keys upon the lapels of his black velvet-collared coat, speaking with an Italian accent.

spans.anchor: The correspondence of that person living in Longridge Road is copied
